title: Finland Caught Between Austerity and a Recovery Too Fragile to Bear It · 17 Aug
keywords: Finland, fiscal policy, austerity, public deficit, economic recovery, GDP growth, unemployment, inflation, welfare state, EU fiscal rules, European Commission, Bank of Finland, Finnish politics, household costs, ageing population
notes: Finland faces a defining political and economic test as its government pushes for spending restraint to contain a swelling public deficit, while the broader economy shows only tentative signs of recovery. GDP growth is forecast at below one percent for 2026, unemployment hovers near ten percent, and inflation, though moderate, has not returned costs to pre-crisis levels. The tension between fiscal consolidation and household fragility is set to dominate Finnish politics through the autumn.
